verdict.rationale: The API covers much of what the UI offers. Documented pieces include the Messages API with streaming, tool use, the MCP connector, code execution, computer use and browser use. It also has Agent Skills for PowerPoint, Word, Excel and PDF, Managed Agents for long-running async work, and Admin and Usage APIs that replace Console tasks by hand. However, several consumer UI features have no documented API equivalent in the evidence: memory across conversations, Projects, scheduled task hand-off, and Claude Design, Slides and Docs. Missing for 10: API equivalents for memory, Projects, scheduling and Design/Slides/Docs; an explicit UI–API parity statement; independent hands-on corroboration of parity.
